Symmetric encryption provides confidentiality by using a shared secret key to transform plaintext into ciphertext before transmission. Only parties that possess the same secret key can decrypt the ciphertext back into plaintext. An eavesdropper who captures the ciphertext but does not have the key cannot readily understand the message, so the communication remains confidential to authorized users.

Brute-force attack tries every possible key or mapping until the correct one is found, whereas cryptanalysis uses available information—such as ciphertext only, known plaintext, chosen plaintext, guessed words, or redundancy—to deduce the key/plaintext or reduce the number of possibilities that must be checked. In short, brute force is exhaustive guessing over the whole key space; cryptanalysis is intelligent analysis exploiting weaknesses or additional information.
